triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Correction to the body (triage, 2026-11-18T02:04Z): "hosted, which runs remote Turso" is **unverified**. The cloud seat's reading on #35028 says only that hosted registers the project's pooled driver as `default`; it did not name the driver. The reading here should also establish which deployments actually run the Turso remote face (`os serve` remote mode, self-hosted, or hosted) before the p1 condition is judged.

triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

**Regraded p2 → p1 by the maintainer's grading principle of 2026-11-18**, accepted in triage's session (「刚才你建议的分级调整，我全部接受」).

The principle, in order:
1. What a new user or a prospect meets first (looks and the main flow), the cloud core (Turso, hosted sign-up and onboarding, hosted install and upgrade, plans) and a developer's first contact come first.
2. Data loss or a permission breach in normal use stays first.
3. Details and rare configurations are improved over time.
4. Internal items are frozen.

Why this card: cloud core: hosted tenants run on Turso remote, so the boolean-text backfill must reach the remote face (triage's earlier "hosted on Turso unverified" note was wrong).

repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbaX2qDxUq9sF93EqqL

Claim amendment (build phase) · 2026-11-18T06:21Z. This amends the claim 6970062028.

The reading is positive (os-dev report 6970820123). On main `958ee035949` (18.6.0), the Turso remote face never runs `SqlDriver.initObjects`. `completeRemoteSchemaSync` (turso-driver.ts:3625-3635) runs only the temporal and codec-residue twins. A probe on the remote face stored `'true'`/`'false'` as TEXT through create, update and updateMany. In that state, `= false`, `= true`, `$ne`, `$in` and count mis-select the rows, and a reboot leaves them unconverted. The local-face control converged the same rows. Shipped writers reach this state on every release up to 18.5.0, so the card's build half is authorised by its own done-when.

Open question from the report, decided at PM discretion. It is an implementation-placement choice with no product or contract face, so no ruling is owed: **option A**. The remote twin takes the legacy-boolean predicate through a protected `SqlDriver` member, the same way the temporal twin takes `sqliteCanonicalDatetimeSql`. That keeps one definition, adds no index export and no Clause-② widening. B (a published export) and C (a copied predicate with a parity pin) were declined for those reasons.

File surface (amended): `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/**` + its tests, plus `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/**`, limited to exposing the existing predicate as a protected member, with no behaviour change on the local face. One changeset covers driver-turso (patch) and driver-sql (patch, if its source moves). Stop on breach and report.
